sentence: This project tests a treatment for glioblastoma that uses small molecules to block a signal in macrophage-based immunotherapy.
This project studies how long non-coding RNA affects the way cells make exosomes.
This project develops light-powered microelectronics that help make drug molecules through electrosynthesis.
This project studies immune system changes in animal models of glioblastoma treated with a vaccine and immune cell therapies.
This project builds computational tools that find the structures of large molecular machines while they move.
This project builds remote tasks that measure early signs of language problems in infants with autism before a clinical diagnosis.
This project studies how impulsivity and the way young adults respond to alcohol are linked.
This project studies how astrocytes change during aging and in a mouse model of Alzheimer's Disease.
This project studies the genomic drivers of acute leukemia and tests ways to treat the disease.
This project studies how bacteria use an adaptive immune system to survive attacks by phages.
This project studies who respiratory viruses affect, how quickly they spread in communities and households, and how well vaccines protect people.
This project tries to find which enzymes and metabolic pathways depend on vitamins and which genetic diseases megavitamin therapies can treat.
This project builds a snapshot hyperspectral imager for microscopy that images many fluorophores at once with less phototoxicity.
This project tests whether epigenetic changes make tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte therapy work better in lung cancer.
This project tests a model of how Alzheimer's biomarkers change over time using imaging of amyloid, tau and neurodegeneration.
This project develops a blood test that finds cancer early by sequencing whole genome DNA in plasma and studying structural variants.
This project develops a nanoparticle carrying two drugs to treat triple negative breast cancer and tests its safety and delivery in animal models.
This project studies how exercise changes aging stem cells through a cell signaling pathway involved in inflammatory responses.
This project tests whether faulty beta-endorphin signaling in the brain links insecure attachment to the effects of childhood maltreatment in a mouse model.
